Charisma
KAH-ris-mah
n. (Greek)
Greek charisma, “a gift of grace, free gift,” from charis (grace, favor); plural charismata. The word designates both saving gifts (eternal life, Rom 6:23) and the diverse gifts of the Spirit distributed to members of the body.

📖 Biblical Definition

Charisma is the New Testament’s precise word for a gift of grace—the Spirit-given endowment freely bestowed on the church and on individual saints for the building up of the body and the accomplishing of God’s purposes. The cognate noun charis (grace, free favor) makes the etymology theologically pointed: every charisma is a graced gift, freely given, not earned, distributed by the Spirit’s sovereign apportioning rather than the recipient’s merit. The word covers a broad semantic range across the NT. At its highest, charisma names the gift of salvation itself: for the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God (to charisma tou theou) is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord (Rom 6:23). Eternal life is the supreme charisma: grace-given, not earned, freely bestowed on those who believe in Christ. The word covers the spiritual gifts distributed to members of the body for the upbuilding of the church. Romans 12:6-8: having then gifts (charismata) differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness. 1 Corinthians 12:4-11 lists nine gifts: word of wisdom, word of knowledge, faith, gifts of healing, working of miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, divers kinds of tongues, interpretation of tongues. 1 Corinthians 12:28-30 lists various offices and gifts: apostles, prophets, teachers, miracles, gifts of healing, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. Ephesians 4:11 lists the gifts of ascended Christ to the church: apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers. 1 Peter 4:10-11: as every man hath received the gift (charisma), even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth. Several structural features mark the doctrine. First, every believer has at least one charisma: as every man hath received the gift; the gifts are distributed across the body, not concentrated in a few. Second, the gifts are diverse: the body has many members, and the Spirit distributes the gifts variously according to His sovereign will (1 Cor 12:11, but all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will). Third, the gifts are given for the body: but the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal (1 Cor 12:7); they are not for private flourishing but for corporate building. Fourth, the gifts must be exercised in love: 1 Cor 13 sits between the two gift-chapters precisely to insist that without love the gifts are nothing and profit nothing. Fifth, the gifts are to be cultivated and stirred up: Paul charges Timothy to stir up the gift of God, which is in thee (2 Tim 1:6). The recovery of biblical charismata is therefore the recovery of the whole-body, diverse, love-grounded, actively-stewarded ministry of every Spirit-equipped saint in the building up of the church.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

(Greek term.) Charisma: gift of grace, free gift; the NT word for the Spirit-given endowments distributed to members of the body for upbuilding, including the supreme charisma of eternal life itself (Rom 6:23); plural charismata.

GIFT, n. — 1. Anything given or bestowed; anything which is voluntarily transferred by one person to another, without compensation. 2. The act of giving or conferring. 3. The right or power of giving or bestowing. 4. In scripture, the gifts of God, including salvation (Rom 6:23), the indwelling Spirit (Acts 2:38; 8:20), and the diverse gifts of the Spirit distributed to members of the body (1 Cor 12).

CHARISMA — (Greek noun, G5486.) Gift of grace, free gift. 17 NT uses; cognate of charis (grace, G5485).

📖 Key Scripture

Romans 6:23 — "For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord."

1 Corinthians 12:4-7 — "Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal."

Romans 12:6 — "Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith."

1 Peter 4:10 — "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Charisma-shaped gifting is corrupted, on one side, by the charismatic-movement excesses that have elevated certain showy gifts (tongues, miracles, prophetic words) above the broader range of NT gifts and treated them as the markers of true spirituality—and on the other by the cessationist over-correction that has so feared the excesses that it has muted the Spirit’s present-age distribution of gifts to the body, against the NT pattern that every believer has a gift and the body functions when every gift is exercised.

expand to see more

The charismatic-movement excesses have, across the past century and especially in their Pentecostal and neo-Pentecostal forms, elevated certain showy gifts (tongues, miraculous healings, prophetic words, falling-in-the-Spirit phenomena) above the broader range of NT gifts and treated them as the markers of true spirituality. The result is a Christianity in which the believer who does not exhibit these particular gifts is implicitly second-class, the church gathering is shaped around the cultivation and display of these gifts, and the broader range of NT charismata (giving, helping, governing, mercy, teaching, exhortation) is muted as comparatively unspectacular. Scripture refuses the hierarchy. 1 Cor 12 explicitly insists that the body needs the diverse gifts; that the comparatively-less-visible gifts (helps, governments) are no less important than the comparatively-more-visible (tongues, miracles); and that no member of the body may say to another I have no need of thee. The recovery is the recovery of the whole NT gift-catalog: every saint gifted, every gift important, the showy and the unshowy alike given for the building up of the body.

The opposite corruption is the cessationist over-correction that has so feared the charismatic-movement excesses that it has muted the Spirit’s present-age distribution of gifts to the body. Some cessationist traditions have effectively dropped the categories of charismata from active church life: the saints are not catechized in the doctrine of gifts; gifts-discernment is not practiced; the body operates largely through the formal offices and the volunteerism of those who happen to step forward, with no systematic recognition that the Spirit has equipped every member with particular gifts for particular ministries. The recovery is the recovery of the doctrine without the excesses: every believer has a charisma, every gift is given for the body, the gifts are diverse and the body needs them all, the gifts are to be exercised in love and stewarded with diligence. The cessationist question of whether some particular gifts (tongues, miracles, prophecy in its foundational-revelatory form) have ceased with the apostolic age is a legitimate intramural Reformed discussion; but the broader pattern of Spirit-distributed charismata to every member of the body is not in question and must be recovered if the church is to function as the body Scripture describes.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek charisma (gift of grace, free gift), cognate with charis (grace); the NT word for the Spirit-given endowments distributed to every believer for the building up of the body, including the supreme charisma of eternal life itself; plural charismata, diverse, given by the Spirit’s sovereign apportioning, exercised in love.

expand to see more

Greek charisma (G5486) — gift of grace, free gift (17 NT uses).

Greek charis (G5485) — grace, free favor (the cognate noun; over 150 NT uses).

Greek charizomai (G5483) — to give freely, to forgive graciously (the cognate verb).

Greek dōrea (G1431) — gift (the cousin term; especially of the gift of the Spirit, Acts 2:38; 8:20; 10:45; 11:17).

Usage

"The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord—the supreme charisma is salvation itself, freely given by grace."

"As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another—1 Pet 4:10 commands the active stewardship of the Spirit’s charismata in the body."

"Charismatic-movement excesses elevate showy gifts; cessationist over-correction mutes the Spirit’s present-age distribution; biblical pattern is every saint gifted, every gift given for the body, exercised in love."
